name: Project: Science Goes Public: New Ways of Communicating Knowledge
description:
If an experience is worth more than a thousand words, why is science communication often confined to traditional, straightforward, and sometimes even paternalistic explanations of scientific phenomena?

This workshop offers a hands-on approach to responsible science communication, equipping students with the skills to design and implement their own experimental programs for creating participatory and engaging experiences. While participation and engagement are key concepts in responsible science communication theories, these must extend beyond theoretical frameworks and be brought into the practical realm. Students will learn how to move beyond mere knowledge transfer of scientific concepts and instead create compelling narratives and immersive experiences that foster the active production of knowledge.

The course provides a comprehensive learning encounter, including two visits to the Deutsches Museum and two moderated concept development sessions for students to develop their own experimental programs. During the sessions at the Deutsches Museum, students will participate in two experimental visitor programs (“Alchemy” and “Microchips under the magnifying glass ”), allowing them to observe, analyse, and reflect on established science communication strategies in action. For their final project, students will design and present a short experimental program that showcases the knowledge and skills they have acquired.

This initiative empowers students to become responsible and innovative science communicators, bridging the gap between their scientific disciplines and the public in a truly participatory and engaging way.
